decisions.reason: Chakravarty (2015) is a replicated target tested on two components in the Pakistan DHS sample: (1) Chakravarty's additional sibling-sex-composition hypothesis (prediction 4, eq. 3), which is confirmed in Table 5 col. 5 (Section V.C), Section V.G, and the Conclusion (Section VII), and (2) Chakravarty's quadratic birth-order interaction specification for prediction 9 (Section V.F, Table 9 cols. 2-3). In Table 9 col. 2, replicating Chakravarty's original specification reproduces a strongly statistically significant gender-by-birth-order interaction (p = .000 jointly) in line with a middle-birth-order peak, but the authors show that Chakravarty's specification omits the gender main effect and that adding the gender dummy in col. 3 eliminates the middle-birth-order peak. Under the codebook's main-message rule, 'statistically successful but flawed' applies only when the methodological critique is the paper's main message; here, the omitted-main-effect critique concerns only one regression specification in Section V.F and is not the main message of the paper or of the Chakravarty comparison (which highlights confirmation of prediction 4 in the Summary and Conclusion). Because prediction 4 is supported while the middle-birth-order peak is rejected once properly specified, the overall outcome for Chakravarty (2015) is 'mixed'.
